notes: SHIP v1.14.362 - RENAME THE OTHER FOUR BANNER RASTERS to match DEPLOY. Completes the convention .361 started, by owner ruling 2026-07-30 ('rename the other four to match'). icons/phantom-banner-{scan,master,ops,handoff}-1170.webp become icons/{SCAN,MASTER,OPS,HANDOFF}-phone@3x.webp. The banner set is now internally consistent again: five files, one convention, -phone@3x.webp. NAMING RULE APPLIED, AND THE ONE PLACE IT REQUIRED A CALL: the pattern was read off DEPLOY as 'uppercase the existing stem, keep the -phone@3x suffix'. That maps scan/ops/handoff unambiguously. MASTER is the one that needed a decision - its existing stem is 'master' but its row label in the app is 'MASTER FILE', and DEPLOY gave no signal either way because its stem and its label were already identical. Shipped as MASTER-phone@3x.webp, preserving the existing stem, because that is the least-inference reading; MASTER-FILE-phone@3x.webp would have invented a name the ruling never used. One-line change if the owner wants the label form instead. TWELVE THINGS MOVE AND NOTHING ELSE: four files (git mv, so history follows each and the raster bytes are untouched - scan 72252, master 50056, ops 49056, handoff 37588, all still 1170x403), four attributes, and four PRECACHE_URLS entries. No art was re-staged, re-encoded or re-cropped. The PRECACHE_URLS list keeps its existing ORDER - the entries were renamed in place rather than resorted, so the diff is four strings, not a reshuffled block. WHY A VERSION BUMP FOR A RENAME - the .361 reasoning, now applied to four files at once: this changes four served asset paths and four precache keys. A client on the old service worker has the old URLs cached and would 404 every new one, so the CACHE_VERSION bump is what makes the swap safe - the new SW builds a fresh cache from the new list and the activate handler deletes the old. A rename without the bump is an offline-boot break. The blast radius here is four of the five banner rows rather than one, which makes the offline check correspondingly more important, not less. '@' IS LEGAL UNENCODED in a path segment (RFC 3986 pchar = unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ':' / '@'), so no percent-encoding is used. Each string and its PRECACHE_URLS counterpart are byte-identical, which is what makes the Cache API match: both resolve against the same base to the same request URL. A mismatch on any one of the four is INVISIBLE ONLINE - the network serves the file regardless - and shows up only as that row falling back to the accent hatch offline. The gate checks all five equalities directly, plus zero residue of any old filename in either live file. WHAT THE OLD NAMES LEAVE BEHIND: nothing live. 'phantom-banner-' now appears in dct-ios.html and sw.js exactly zero times; the remaining occurrences across BATCH-VERIFY.md, design/OWNER-RULINGS.md and this file's own history are prose describing what was shipped when, which stays accurate as history and is deliberately not rewritten. BATCH POSITION - FLAGGED: this is the EIGHTH ship in batch .355-.362, TWO past the CALL-0 six-ship cap, on a batch that was already due on two independent grounds before .361 (the cap itself, and HIGH-risk .359). Shipped on direct owner instruction; precedent exists for stacking past the cap by owner decision (.208 through .212 ran to eleven). The consolidated device pass is now two ships overdue and nothing further should ship before it clears. GATES: three-stamp lockstep; inline JS compiles (4 of 4 blocks) plus sw.js; CSS braces balanced in all 12 style blocks; dct-ios.html diff is five lines (four src attributes plus the stamp) with nothing else carrying markup; all five renamed files exist on disk at their new paths and are precached under byte-identical strings; zero residue of any old banner filename in either live file; the .359 acceptance checks re-run green (5 banner rows, 9 wall cells); the .359 rows, OPS wall, handlers, registry and CSS are untouched. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) badge reads v1.14.362. (2) BUILD: ALL FIVE rows still show their photographs. Any row showing the diagonal accent hatch means that row's rename broke its reference - and the hatch is doing exactly its job by telling you which one. (3) CLEAR THE SERVICE WORKER, airplane mode, hard reload - all five photographs still render offline. THIS IS THE ONLY CHECK THAT PROVES THE RENAME: an online browser fetches every new path from the network even if all four precache entries were wrong, so an online eyeball cannot fail here no matter what is broken. (4) ?legacy=1 unchanged. ROLLBACK: revert this commit - it restores all four old filenames, their eight references and their precache entries together, and no raster bytes ever changed. .361 (the DEPLOY rename) reverts independently.
